arm_ii_injection.bug_found_and_fixed: eval/reph_inject.py's _walk() silently dropped a log's trailing <3-byte remainder (found against fwdplainc_tex_r1/fwdplainc_trans_r1, which end mid-header) -- AssertionError on first attempt, both bags. First fix attempt (keying a new trailing-entry check on the loop variable `i`) introduced a SECOND bug: it double-appended an identical skip entry on any log whose LAST record is itself truncated (the pre-existing 'i + f.length > n' branch already appends its own entry and breaks without advancing `i`) -- found against fwdc_tex_r1 (+16 bytes on strip()). Fixed by keying on out[-1][1] ('covered_end') instead of `i`. Both regressions added to eval/reph_inject_test.py (12/12 pass). Verified the fix changed NOTHING already computed: reinjected.bin == reinjected_v2.bin (the round-trip template) and arms/fwdc_tex_r1/heading/injected.bin == a fresh fixed-code reinjection, both exact byte-for-byte matches -- neither bug was present in the code when the round-trip Replay compare, arm (i) (18 bags), or fwdc_tex_r1's arm (ii) were run; the two originally-failing bags were simply re-run once fixed, and the other 16 bags never exercised the new code paths at all.
arm_ii_injection.input_count_note: Every arm (ii) record set = measurement_models.forward_events(trial, 'heading')'s full valid output (matches the preregistration's own definition of the input, section 5), NOT the stored fgo_heading/fwd_stats.json 'psi_valid' count, which is smaller for every bag checked (e.g. fwdc_tex_r1: 9654 vs 9539, a 1.2% difference). Partially characterised, not fully: only 1 of fwdc_tex_r1's 9654 valid frames falls before its first IMU sample (10.696 s) and 13 fall after t=348s (near landing); that accounts for 14 of the 115-frame gap, not all of it. The remaining ~101 frames' exclusion from fgo_heading's own count is NOT verified here -- stated as an open item, not asserted as explained.
arm_ii_injection.evo_ape_a_nan_on_fwdplainc_blank: fwdplainc_blank_r1/r2/r3's arm (ii) result_evo_a_cruise is NaN: evo_ape reports 'Degenerate covariance rank, Umeyama alignment is not possible' because the replayed EKF3 position estimate is EXACTLY (0,0) for every sample in the pinned cruise window (checked directly: est range x=[0,0], y=[0,0]). This is a known characteristic of this no-flow-signal floor condition, not specific to arm (ii) or to this tool -- arm (i)'s baseline on the same bag also spends most of the flight in const_pos_mode (horiz_pos_rel true only 6.3% of samples) and its own evo -a (cruise) number (43.45 m) reflects a frozen-near-origin estimate against a moving ground truth, not a meaningful ATE. Phase 4's own scoring already anticipates this by computing SEPARATE 'failure metrics' (final displacement ratio, divergence onset) for transition/blank bags alongside evo -a (cruise); the same failure metrics (eval/three_way_eval.failure_metrics()) are used for arm (i)/(ii) in the final scoring step, not a substitute number for the NaN.
